title: Quiet in the barn
text: The night in the barn passed peacefully, only an owl hooting on a beam. Everyone slept in the hay like kings.

title: Holes in the roof
text: Rain broke through the thatch and soaked part of the bedding. Half the crew slept wet.

title: The village dog
text: A shaggy mutt barked at the fence all night and by morning made friends with the crew for a bit of bacon.

title: The child with milk
text: A girl from the next farm brought a jug of milk and asked if it's true you're bandits. She got bread and kept the secret.

title: The shepherd
text: A shepherd drove his flock close by. One sheep got lost and ended up in your yard. The shepherd pretended not to see it.

title: The village fair
text: A small fair was held in the village. Stalls of hides, cheese and honey tempted, and the peasants' pockets were full.

title: The priest of Taal
text: A village priest of Taal passed with a basket of herbs and asked little: not to light fires in the forest. Nobody objected.

title: The lost cow
text: A cow stepped through the fence and walked right into your camp. Nobody managed to lead her back until she'd been milked.

title: The tax collector
text: The count's tax collector rode through the village with two henchmen and took what he could. The peasants' faces were stone.

title: Crop-wrecking hail
text: Hail destroyed part of the crops and many roofs. The peasants wept and the crew felt unwelcome.

title: Harvest festival
text: The village celebrated harvest home. Songs, dances and ale flowed freely. The crew stood aside but someone pressed a jug on them.

title: Wolves
text: Wolves howled in the nearby forest all night. Horses tugged at their tethers and the guards watched the fires till dawn.

title: The missing sheep
text: Villagers searched for a lost sheep with lanterns. The crew kept quiet and the sheep served as a reserve for two days.

title: The old widow
text: A widow from the next cottage knocked asking for firewood. In return she gave a sack of dried apples and a tale of old times.

title: The strange stone
text: A stone with an engraved mark nobody recognised lay by the well. The villagers gave it a wide berth.

title: The miller
text: The miller brought a sack of flour and asked if you needed any. His eyes betrayed that he's eager to sell goods he shouldn't.

title: The burning haystack
text: Someone set a haystack ablaze in a neighbour's field. The village rushed to put it out and a few followers, uninvited, helped.

title: The wedding
text: A wedding was held in the village. The whole neighbourhood celebrated till midnight and by dawn nobody remembered who was who.

title: The lost calf
text: A calf broke from its pen and bolted into the forest. Your people caught it within an hour. The owner gave cheese as a reward.

title: The drunken carter
text: A drunken carter overturned his wagon on the road and barrels rolled into a ditch. Nobody counted how many there were.

title: The sick horse
text: A neighbouring farmer's horse fell sick and died. The farmer despaired and the meat had to be used quickly.

title: The blacksmith
text: The village smith sharpened your knives for free. He refused payment because "we all have our sins here."

title: The lost traveller
text: A traveller with a map was looking for the road to Altdorf. The crew pointed him on his way and he left a few small coins.

title: A feud over a boundary
text: Two neighbours quarrelled over a boundary and threw stones. Your people placed bets on who'd win.

title: The storks
text: Storks flew away and the villagers claimed winter would come early. A few followers began looking for warmer clothes.

title: The livestock market
text: Hens, geese and piglets were sold at the village market. One follower returned with a hen under his arm and an innocent look.

title: The path through the fields
text: A path through the fields led from the road to your camp but nobody came by it. The villagers had their own affairs.

title: Chimney smoke
text: The smell of baking bread drifted from a nearby cottage chimney. A few followers crept over for a loaf.

title: The forester's visit
text: The count's forester checked whether you were burning fires in the forest. Everything looked fine so he left, wishing you a good night.

title: Spooked horses
text: Something frightened the horses in the stable. The whole village ran out with lanterns but found nothing. Luckily the crew wasn't to blame.

title: The armed rider
text: A lone rider in armour rode through the village without a word. The villagers shut their doors and the crew held its breath.

title: News of war
text: A messenger reached the village with news of greenskins on the eastern frontier. The peasants began hiding grain and some of the crew would rather move on.

title: The burnt cottage
text: A cottage at the edge of the village burned and its inhabitants vanished. The villagers say it's the work of unclean powers and you found coins in the ashes.

title: Children in the haystack
text: Children playing hide-and-seek in a haystack found one of your men asleep inside. He promised them two plums for silence.

title: The reeve's feast
text: The reeve gave a feast for guests from town and invited the whole camp. The crew played respectable merchants and the food was excellent.

title: The geese
text: A flock of geese attacked your man who tried to approach. Everyone laughed and he sulked for a long time.

title: The well
text: The village well dried up and the peasants had to draw water from your stream. The crew received a few small gifts.

title: The black cat superstition
text: A black cat crossed the camp and half the crew began looking for wood to make a protective sign.

title: A quiet funeral
text: The village buried an old man. Everyone followed the coffin in silence and the crew doffed caps and bowed in respect.

title: The village fiddler
text: The village fiddler played in the open air in the evening and half the village came to listen. The music was awful and everyone had a great time.

title: The peddler
text: A travelling pedlar with a wagon of goods set up a stall by the road. The crew spotted a few things that could come in handy.

title: The ghost rumour
text: Children spoke of a ghost in the abandoned mill. The elders shushed them but at night none went out of their huts.

title: The farmwife with eggs
text: A farmwife sold eggs from a basket and haggled fiercely. The crew got half a basket at half price because "men need to eat."

title: A drunken farmhand
text: A drunken farmhand waves a pitchfork and shouts threats outside your camp. Someone will be hurt soon.
okText: The bodyguard took the pitchfork with one hand and poured him milk with the other. The farmhand left ashamed.

title: Village hooligans
text: A gang of village hooligans looks for a quarrel with strangers. If nobody stops them the village will never forget you.
okText: The bodyguard stood before them and looked. The hooligans lowered their heads and the boldest offered friendship and lent hay.

title: The horse thief
text: A horse thief crept into a neighbour's stable and now tries to involve you. If he's caught he'll point at you.
okText: The shadow intercepted the thief in the dark, took his haul and sent him the other way, and the horses returned to their place with a reward for the finder.

title: The village informer
text: A village informer began sniffing around your camp and writes everything on a slip. In the morning he'll go to the manor.
okText: The shadow borrowed the informer's slip and returned it in the morning with new, very boring notes. The informer no longer wanted to get involved.

title: Foxes in the henhouse
text: A fox got into the neighbour's henhouse and the noise woke the whole village. If nobody shoots it the villagers will start looking for culprits.
okText: The marksman hit the fox with one shot from a long way off. The villagers rejoiced and left two hens in thanks.

title: The deer in the grain
text: A stag ate half a field of wheat and the villagers want it dead but lack skill. The count forbids hunting.
okText: The marksman killed the stag quietly and cleanly. The villagers feasted and swore silence, and the crew got the best cuts.

title: A neighbourly feud
text: Two village families have been quarrelling for a week and drawing in more people. The village is a step from a brawl.
okText: The provocateur convinced both sides that a third party was to blame and everyone mocked a stranger together. The crew left with a generous gift for "mediation".

title: The travelling juggler
text: A juggler competes with your man for the attention of a village audience. Losing means losing standing.
okText: The provocateur made a laughing stock of the juggler and then invited him to perform together. The crowd paid double.

title: The sick boy
text: The farmer's son has a high fever and there's no physician within a day's ride. The father begs for your help.
okText: The scavenger used herbs from his bag and a few old tricks. The boy broke into a sweat and recovered. The farmer gave food and silver.

title: The collapsed cellar
text: The cellar of a village house collapsed and the peasants can't reach their stores. Winter is near.
okText: The scavenger dug out everything he could in three hours and left some of the stores "as a keepsake".

title: The merchant's broken wagon
text: A merchant's wagon broke down on the road and the goods lie in a ditch. He fears someone will rob him.
okText: The carter fixed the axle in an hour and reloaded the goods. The merchant gave a generous tip and promised to recommend you to acquaintances.

title: The bridge inspection
text: The count's guards inspect people on the bridge and search wagons. Your supplies must get to the other side.
okText: The carter knew a ford below the bridge and brought the wagon there. The inspection saw nothing and the supplies reached the other bank.

title: The count's fence
text: The count ordered a fence put up across the village fields, cutting the village off from the forest. The peasants are furious and look for someone to destroy it.
okText: The arsonist burned the fence in a night, without casualties or trace. The peasants paid him secretly with gratitude in their eyes.

title: The old mill
text: The abandoned mill by the river is starting to collapse and endangers the village. Someone must pull it down before it kills a child.
okText: The arsonist brought the mill down in a controlled blast and saved the village. In the rubble he found forgotten caches of flour and coins.

title: The bandits' trail
text: The scout noticed tracks that shouldn't be here: fresh, from many men, towards the village. Someone is preparing a raid.
okText: The scout followed the trail, warned the villagers and led them to an ambush. The raid failed and the grateful village rewarded the crew generously.

title: The lost pilgrim
text: A pilgrim lost his way and wanders the forest. If nobody finds him the wolves will.
okText: The scout found the pilgrim before dawn and led him to the village. In thanks he got a blessing and a handful of coins.

title: A village lawsuit
text: Two peasants dragged each other to court over a field boundary. Both sides seek someone to forge a deed of ownership.
okText: The fence sold both sides "deeds" and brokered a settlement. Both felt justice was done and the crew had full pockets.

title: A valuable find
text: A peasant found an old coin in the field and doesn't know what it's worth. A dealer offers three coppers.
okText: The fence recognised the rare coin, persuaded the peasant to an honest price and took a commission. Everyone left satisfied.

title: Plague in the byre
text: The villagers have sick cows and seek someone who knows. If the cattle die the village will starve.
okText: The healer identified the cause, prepared ointment and a drink and within two days the cows recovered. The village paid him in cheese and silver.

title: The alleged witch
text: Villagers point at old Hilde and want her burned as a witch. If no one reacts a pyre will smoke.
okText: The healer played the inquisitor, questioned Hilde and found her innocent "on the evidence". The villagers paid for the verdict.

title: The farmhand's challenge
text: The strongest farmhand in the village challenged your man to wrestle. Losing means losing honour, winning means hostility.
okText: The duellist accepted and after a few flashy holds let the farmhand "almost win". The village adored the guest.

title: A duel over a girl
text: Two farmhands challenged each other to a duel over a village girl. If blood is spilled the count's guard will arrive sooner than necessary.
okText: The duellist acted as second, taught them to use wooden swords and settled the dispute in a jesting manner. The village had a good time.

title: The stranger at the inn
text: A lone stranger with a pulled-down hood sits drinking in silence in the village inn. He speaks to no one.

title: The stranger again
text: The hooded stranger came to the camp and laid a purse on the ground. He says: "I need a favour and I'll remember."

title: The lost casket
text: Children found a casket with a broken lock in the field and brought it to the camp. Someone is looking for it.

title: The casket's owner
text: The reeve came to the camp and asked about the casket. He promises a reward but unease shows in his eyes.

title: The runaway farmhand
text: A farmhand begs for shelter from the count's steward. He says he stole a piece of ham from the kitchen and just wanted a taste.

title: The steward searches
text: The count's steward rode up and asks about the runaway farmhand. He promises silver but adds that hiding him carries a penalty.

title: Crackle of the fire
text: Around the fire several followers told tales of vampires and water-spirits. Until morning nobody wanted to go out to relieve himself alone.

title: Gathering mushrooms
text: Village girls gathered mushrooms right by the camp. Your men pretended to be woodcutters, but one of them watched suspiciously long.

title: A pigeon with a message
text: A pigeon carrying a letter to the manor lost its bearings and landed in camp. The note concerned upcoming taxes.

title: The flock of geese
text: Geese marched through the camp with a racket and took half a bucket of grain. Someone had to chase them.

title: Strange tracks
text: In the morning hoof prints of horse size but with three toes were found near the camp. The villagers crossed themselves and left.

title: The missing boy
text: A boy from the village went missing and the whole neighbourhood searched. One of yours found him sleeping in a haystack and took him home.

title: The swollen stream
text: The stream swelled after rain and crossing it took time. Nobody complained because the water was cold and clean.

title: An offering to Taal
text: Villagers left a bundle of grain and a jug of honey by the forest as an offering to Taal. The crew dared not touch it.

title: Crows in the field
text: A flock of crows settled on the field and the peasants came out with a racket to scare them off. In the confusion it was easy to take a little from the pantry.

title: Procession of children
text: Village children carried little lanterns and sang a winter song. The crew didn't know whether to laugh or cry.

title: The barn burned
text: A neighbour's barn was struck by lightning and burned. The whole village fought the fire and the crew got thanks for helping.

title: The broken axle
text: The wagon axle snapped and the smith had to be called. A day lost, but the smith gave a good price for help with a small job.

title: A heathen song
text: From the forest depths came singing in an unknown tongue. The villagers stopped their ears and your people didn't sleep till dawn.

title: A bet over grain
text: Two peasants bet on who could toss a sickle higher. Your man won and got a sack of oats.

title: The count's men
text: The count's men set up barriers on the road and check everyone. The village is stirred up but you have a good hiding place.

title: Village festival
text: The village celebrates a festival of Rhya. Everyone dances, bakes bread in the shape of ears of corn and gives it to guests.

title: Thunder
text: Thunder shook the ground and several cows died in the pasture. The villagers speak of the gods' wrath.

title: The broken leg
text: A peasant broke his leg at the cart and his family was left without help. The crew shared its supplies.

title: The apiary
text: A neighbour's apiary was raided by a bear. The peasant ran about with a pot while your people watched from a safe distance.

title: The slaughter
text: The villagers slaughtered a pig and invited neighbours for black pudding and sausages. The crew got its share too.

title: Ravens over the field
text: Ravens circled over the field where a battle was once fought. The elders whispered that something is waking there.

title: The late courier
text: An imperial courier rode through the village and left a lost letter on a bench. It begged to be kept.

title: Two wagons
text: Two wagons collided on the road and the carters began fighting. The crew watched and after the brawl gathered up the remains of the load.

title: The buried treasure
text: A village grandfather told a tale of treasure buried under an old oak. Several followers dug through the night and found only roots.

title: The lost scythe
text: A scythe borrowed from a peasant vanished in the grass. They searched till evening and found it only in the morning.

title: The soldier's return
text: A soldier returning from the war stopped in the village. He told of battles and showed scars while your people listened breathlessly.

title: The horse paddock
text: A farmer showed your people his horses and offered one for sale. The mare was beautiful but the price too high.

title: Smoke towards the sky
text: Columns of smoke rise far on the horizon. Nobody knows whether it's a fire or a raid but the villagers locked their doors.

title: The threshing
text: Villagers threshed grain all night by torchlight. The crew helped and got a sack of grain for it.

title: The storyteller
text: A wandering storyteller sat under a linden tree and told tales. The whole village gathered and you made good use of the crowd.

title: The pike in the pond
text: The villagers caught a giant pike and shared it with the whole village. The crew got a piece too.

title: The hay is gone
text: By morning a neighbour's haystack had vanished. The villagers suspected the crew but couldn't prove anything.

title: An angry mob
text: Villagers gathered with pitchforks because someone told them your people steal children. If no one calms them there'll be bloodshed.
okText: The bodyguard stood before the crowd with folded arms and asked who wanted to check first. Nobody did and the villagers dispersed ashamed.

title: The overturned wagon
text: A wagon of roof tiles overturned on the road pinning the carter. If nobody lifts the wagon the man will die.
okText: The bodyguard lifted the wagon on his back, pulled out the carter and got a purse and a promise of a favour from the rescued man.

title: A theft in the night
text: Someone quietly steals from your supplies, one sack a day. Nobody has seen him yet.
okText: The shadow kept watch all night, caught the thief and it turned out to be a peasant out of hunger. The shadow made him an informant and got a handful of news.

title: A trail behind the camp
text: Someone in the dark has followed your tracks for hours, stopping when you stop.
okText: The shadow came up from behind, seized the tracker by the throat and learned a bounty hunter had sent him. The letter lifted from him was worth the trouble.

title: The poacher
text: The count's forester is hunting poachers and asks about your arrows. Without a good answer there'll be trouble.
okText: The marksman showed him a few hares caught "in snares", invited him to supper and sent him off with a sack of meat. The forester suspected nothing.

title: The wolf at the sheep
text: A wolf prowled round the fold and the villagers fear for the flock. The shot must be sure and attract no one's attention.
okText: The marksman killed the wolf with one shot from a distance. The shepherd paid in the pelt and a few shillings and the village hung it on a wall as a trophy.

title: Village gossip
text: A rumour spreads through the village that the crew steals and kills. The villagers begin bolting their doors.
okText: The provocateur spread his own rumour that it was a rival crew's doing. The village calmed and the "informant" was paid.

title: The drunken revel
text: Drunken villagers gathered at the inn intending to go to the camp and "clear things up". They must be occupied with something else.
okText: The provocateur organised a drinking and singing contest and the villagers forgot about the camp by morning. The crew got a loan "for the road ahead".

title: The lost tools
text: A farmer lost all his tools in a storm. Without them he can't sow and all his neighbours depend on it.
okText: The scavenger found all the tools within a day, repaired the broken and made some new from scraps. The farmer paid in food and silver.

title: Rusty iron
text: An old armour and rusted swords were ploughed up in a field. The villagers don't know what to do with them.
okText: The scavenger cleaned and mended what could be saved, sold it to the smith and gave half to the villagers. Nobody asked about origin.

title: Barrels in the ditch
text: Barrels of salt lie in a ditch beside the road. Someone hid or lost them and the count's men ask about them this morning.
okText: The carter took the barrels before the count's men arrived, hid them in a barn and sold the salt in a neighbouring village at a good price.

title: The guarded wagon
text: A wagon with an unlabelled load stands on the road with a guard asleep beside it. If someone wakes him there'll be trouble, if not, a chance.
okText: The carter drove the wagon away without noise, leaving the guard in blissful sleep. The load turned out valuable.

title: The blocked road
text: A huge boulder blocked the village road after a landslide. The peasants have tried to move it for three days.
okText: The arsonist laid a charge and split the boulder into pieces. The villagers saw a miracle in it and offered the crew fresh food.

title: The count's stable
text: The count's stable holds horses the crew could use. The stableman guards them but is greedy.
okText: The arsonist started a small fire in the byre next door and led out two horses in the confusion. The sale brought good money.

title: The new field
text: Someone ploughed a field in the night and sowed something strange. The villagers are afraid and the field looks ritual.
okText: The scout examined the field, recognised an ordinary blend of herbs and calmed the villagers. In thanks he got payment and a tip about hidden roads.

title: The abandoned cottage
text: An abandoned cottage stands in the forest nearby. The crew could shelter there but nobody knows who's been using it.
okText: The scout carefully checked the cottage, removed the traps and found hidden food and a few coins from previous occupants.

title: The forged deed
text: Someone is trying to use a forged deed to take a neighbour's land. The matter may come for you because the seal looks familiar.
okText: The fence examined the document, pointed out the flaws in detail and demanded a fee for the "expert opinion". The peasant regained his land and the crew got paid.

title: Selling wool
text: A peasant has a large stock of wool he can't sell because of a local merchant's monopoly. He seeks a middleman.
okText: The fence found a buyer in the next town, negotiated the price and took a commission. The peasant was happy and the monopolist furious.

title: The lost soul
text: A peasant claims his dead father haunts him at night. The family asks for help.
okText: The healer performed an "exorcism" with salt, smoke and three prayers. The father fell silent and the family paid generously.

title: The poisoned herd
text: A neighbouring well was poisoned and cattle die. The villagers suspect evil magic.
okText: The healer found a natural cause, pointed out a harmful herb in the water and cleaned the well. The village paid him in meat and silver.

title: The pitchfork duel
text: Two peasants duel with pitchforks over a daughter's honour. Someone will die soon.
okText: The duellist stepped in with grace, disarmed both in one move and proposed settling it with ale. The village hailed him a hero.

title: The quarterstaff contest
text: Young villagers held a staff contest and ask your man to demonstrate. Losing would shame the crew.
okText: The duellist beat them all with a smile and then gave a few lessons. The villagers repaid him with bread and coins.

title: The wounded wanderer
text: A wounded wanderer with a sword at his side lies on the road. He says robbers attacked him and begs for water.

title: The wanderer repays
text: The wanderer recovered and revealed he is a local knight's son. He promises a good word to his father and leaves a reward.

title: The found locket
text: A child found a gold locket in the grass with a name engraved. The crew examined it carefully.

title: The noblewoman seeks
text: A young noblewoman rode in and asks about a locket from her late mother. She'll pay any price.

title: The priest's visit
text: A priest of Sigmar stopped for the night and mentioned at supper that he's hunting heretics. He looked at you longer than was proper.

title: The priest returns
text: The priest returned with guards and says he found a dangerous heretic in the next village. He asks for help searching the forest.

title: The scream in the night
text: A wild scream rang out in the village at night and in the morning nobody would speak of it. It seems someone is hiding something.

title: The truth emerges
text: A peasant admitted that someone in his family fell ill with a strange sickness. He asks you to tell no one and pays for silence.

title: The falling star
text: A shooting star flashed across the sky and fell somewhere in the fields. The villagers whisper of an omen.

title: A piece of the sky
text: At the spot where the star fell a piece of strange heavy stone was found. An alchemist from town will pay any price.

title: A chilly morning
text: Dew covered the ground and breath rose in steam. Everyone got up stiff but the fire still glowed well.

title: Storm over the fields
text: A storm swept over the fields with crash and downpour. The crew sat in the barn watching the sky torn by lightning.

title: The full moon
text: The full moon shone so bright one could read by it. The guards saw everything, but you were as visible as on the palm of a hand.

title: Morning mist
text: Mist covered the fields and the road. Villagers heading to work passed within two steps of you without noticing.

title: The owl
text: An owl sat on a beam and stared at you all night. Old folk say it's a bad omen but in the morning it flew off.

title: An accidental guest
text: A wandering merchant passed by and asked the way. He told news from town for a few coppers and moved on.

title: Singing farmhands
text: Farmhands returned from the inn with a song on their lips. Several fell into a ditch and slept, the rest went on.

title: Bad luck with the wagon
text: The wagon wheel fell into a hole and the axle snapped. Several hours had to be spent on repairs.

title: The cunning fox
text: A fox crept into the camp and vanished with a piece of meat. Nobody managed to catch it but everyone admired its skill.

title: The parson's visit
text: The parson came by with a basket asking for donations to fix the church roof. He got small coin and blessed the crew.

title: A cold wind
text: A cold wind howled in the chimney and the shutters creaked. Nobody slept peacefully.

title: Neighbourly help
text: A neighbour helped fix the roof and wanted nothing in return except to be remembered. A good man.

title: Procession of sheep
text: A flock of sheep crossed the road with a shepherd and dog behind it. For an hour nobody could get through.

title: The tethered horse
text: Villagers left a horse tied to a fence and went to the inn. The horse stood quietly all night and nobody claimed it.

title: The drunken priest
text: The village priest returned from a wedding staggering and singing psalms. The crew escorted him to the parsonage.

title: Digging a ditch
text: Villagers dug a drainage ditch beside your camp. In the process they unearthed a handful of old coins and a few bones.

title: The young merchant
text: A young merchant stopped at the camp and praised his wares. The crew bought a few trinkets and heard the news.

title: The oak aflame
text: Lightning struck an old oak which burned like a torch. Until morning the embers glowed red while people whispered of Taal's wrath.

title: Two horses
text: Two horses ran across the field without riders. The villagers caught one, the other vanished into the forest.

title: The river floods
text: The river overflowed and water flooded the meadows. The crew had to move camp higher but found a good spot there.

title: The book in the barn
text: An old book written in an unknown language was found in the barn. The villagers wanted to burn it but the crew took it.

title: Sunday
text: The whole village went to church and the streets were empty. The crew could freely cross the village and look around.

title: A cloud of gnats
text: A cloud of gnats hung over the camp allowing nobody to sleep. By morning everyone was swollen and irritable.

title: The messenger's news
text: A messenger in the count's colours paused to say bandits roam the area. The crew thanked him and kept straight faces.

title: The graveyard
text: The crew camped near the village graveyard. The night was quiet but some claimed to hear steps on the graves.

title: The reapers' song
text: Reapers sang all night by torchlight. The crew fell asleep to the rhythmic sound of scythes.

title: The marketplace
text: A market was held in the nearby town. The crew sent two men who returned with full purses but visibly nervous.

title: The live billy goat
text: A peasant with a billy goat on a string asked if anyone would buy it. The goat was angry and stubborn but had plenty of meat.

title: The friar's visit
text: A wandering friar in a grey habit asked for lodging. He told beautiful stories and in the morning left behind a few useful tips.

title: The drunken knight
text: A drunken knight rode into the camp on horseback bellowing that you're outlaws. If no one silences him he'll draw the village.
okText: The bodyguard pulled the knight from his horse, handed him a cup of water and escorted him away. In the morning the knight apologised and left a purse as "compensation".

title: Brawl at the inn
text: A brawl broke out at the inn and one of yours is in the middle. If he isn't pulled out he'll end up in a dungeon.
okText: The bodyguard walked into the inn, grabbed his man with one hand and carried him out as if nothing had happened. He collected thanks.

title: Bandit ambush
text: Bandits planned an ambush on the road to the village and your people are due to pass that way at dawn.
okText: The shadow detected the ambush, circled round behind, disarmed the bandits in the dark and took their loot.

title: The cryptic sign
text: A sign painted in blood appeared on your fence. The villagers look away.
okText: The shadow recognised a local band's signature in the mark and sent them word that the crew seeks no trouble. The mark disappeared.

title: The rampaging boar
text: A boar charged into the field and is destroying the crop, attacking anyone who approaches. The villagers fear it.
okText: The marksman shot the boar from a safe distance. The village held a feast and the crew got the best cuts and some sausages.

title: The strayed herd
text: A herd of cows escaped the pen and runs towards the forest. Without quick action they'll fall prey to wolves.
okText: The marksman stopped the herd with a precise shot into the ground ahead of the lead cow and the villagers thanked him with milk and silver.

title: The embarrassed reeve
text: The reeve invites you to a meeting to decide what to do about the camp. Everyone eyes you askance.
okText: The provocateur delivered a speech on loyalty to the count and the common enemy and the reeve and villagers invited the crew to a shared table.

title: The village market
text: At the village fair traders squabble over spots. The commotion can be exploited or turned into a brawl.
okText: The provocateur began a quarrel at one end of the market while at the other the crew gathered a few things before anyone noticed.

title: The broken mill
text: The village mill stopped because a wheel cracked. Without flour the village won't survive winter.
okText: The scavenger fixed the wheel with salvaged planks and the miller gave a sack of flour and a few shillings in thanks.

title: The abandoned wagon
text: An abandoned wagon without horses stands on the road. Some crates lie inside and nobody claims it.
okText: The scavenger examined the wagon, took apart what he could and carried the crates to camp. Inside were supplies and a few coins.

title: Forbidden trade
text: Villagers want to sell their salt outside the count's monopoly and look for a way to move it across the border.
okText: The carter organised a night run along hidden trails and got a good commission.

title: The ruined road
text: Rain wrecked the road and wagons sink in the mud. The villagers need someone who knows the local paths.
okText: The carter led several wagons by an alternative road and the villagers paid for the guidance. The crew gained a reputation as people to be trusted.

title: The old haystack
text: Near the camp stands an old haystack where someone hid something valuable. If set alight from the right side everything will vanish.
okText: The arsonist extracted the treasure from the hay and set it alight from afar to hide the traces. The treasure was worth the trouble.

title: The old well
text: The villagers want to fill in an old well said to hold something unwholesome. It must be done so that nothing comes out.
okText: The arsonist filled the well, lit a smoky mixture and closed the lid. The villagers breathed easy and paid for the peace.

title: The new road
text: The road through the forest became too dangerous for merchants. The villagers seek an alternative.
okText: The scout charted a new road through fields and marshes and the villagers paid for the reconnaissance.

title: The wolf den
text: The scout found a wolf den not far from the village. If the wolves go hunting there'll be slaughter.
okText: The scout set a trap and drove the wolves from the village. The villagers thanked him with meat and coins.

title: The peasant's debt
text: A peasant owes the innkeeper money and cannot pay. The innkeeper threatens to take his land.
okText: The fence negotiated payment in instalments and the innkeeper got the crew's "guarantee". The peasant regained peace and the crew gained trust.

title: The wanted notice
text: A wanted notice bearing the likeness of one of yours appeared in the village. If someone sees it there'll be trouble.
okText: The fence swapped the poster for an identical one with another name and added "innocent". Nobody noticed.

title: The rash
text: A child has a strange rash and the mother begs for help. The villagers talk of cursed blood.
okText: The healer recognised an ordinary rash, prescribed herbal baths and calmed the village. The mother paid him what she could.

title: The barren soil
text: One peasant's fields have borne nothing for three years. He hopes for a miracle or at least good advice.
okText: The healer scattered "luck powder" on the field and advised changing the crop. Next year's harvest pleased everyone and the crew was paid.

title: The jealous husband
text: A jealous husband wants to challenge one of yours because he looked at his wife. The matter is innocent but the husband is stubborn.
okText: The duellist disarmed the husband with a smile and invited him for a drink. They parted as friends.

title: The village tournament
text: The village holds a tournament of staves and sabres and offers a prize to the winner. They'd like your man to show off.
okText: The duellist won the tournament gracefully, gave half the prize to the loser and won the hearts of the spectators.

title: The night rider
text: Someone galloped through the village at night and tossed a satchel into the yard. He didn't stop.

title: The satchel opened
text: Inside the satchel documents sealed with a local noble's crest and a few shillings were found. Someone will look for it.

title: The strange wagon
text: An unknown wagon stands by the forest with no driver. The horses are calm but the load is covered with a tarpaulin.

title: The driver turns up
text: The driver returned in trouble: robbers attacked him and took the load. He asks for help recovering it, for generous pay.

title: The manor's dovecote
text: A pigeon from the manor lost its way and landed in camp. The note on its leg carries an coded message.

title: The cipher solved
text: The message was decoded: the manor plans to send soldiers to the village. You can warn the villagers or sell the news.

title: The motherless child
text: A small girl sits by your fire and won't leave. She says nothing, only looks.

title: The girl's family
text: A peasant came for the girl with tears in his eyes and thanked the crew with gifts. His wife died that night.

title: The moneylender's loan
text: The village moneylender offers you a loan on the spot. The terms look favourable.

title: Repayment and interest
text: The moneylender came for repayment with a surprisingly high interest. He has two burly men with him.

title: The old soldier
text: An old soldier with a wooden leg passed through the village telling of the battles at Altdorf. The crew listened with respect.

title: Hailstorm
text: Hail the size of hens' eggs hammered the barn roof. By morning the fields were ruined and the villagers gloomy.

title: The lost lad
text: A lad lost himself in the fields and ended up at the camp. He got bread and in the morning the crew took him back to the village.

title: The wild bird
text: A great bird landed on the barn roof and shrieked hoarsely. Everyone argued whether it was an eagle or a vulture and by morning it flew away.

title: Spring rain
text: Warm rain fell all night washing the dust off the roads. In the morning the air smelled of earth and horses.

title: The false monk
text: A monk with an outstretched hand begged alms but a sword poked out from under the habit. The crew asked no questions.

title: The strzyga's procession
text: Villagers claimed to have seen a vampire walking the path. In the morning only the tracks of a large dog were found.

title: Winter stores
text: Villagers gathered stores for winter and came asking for help with the harvest. The crew helped and got a share of the crop.

title: Trouble with the ox
text: A farmer's ox tore loose and wrecked half the yard. The crew caught it and got a reward in sausage.

title: The unexpected wedding
text: Two followers from different sides of the camp suddenly got engaged and invited everyone to the wedding. A chance for fun.

title: Rubbish by the road
text: Someone left a heap of rubbish by the road with quite useful things among it. The scavengers had a field day.

title: The village fortune teller
text: An old woman told fortunes with cards in the square and your man went to check his future. He came back pale as a wall.

title: A small fire
text: The campfire got out of hand and some of the supplies burned. Everyone insisted it wasn't their fault.

title: Rumours of an army
text: A trader brought word to the village that an army is marching north. Everyone began packing their valuables.

title: The harvest
text: The crew helped with the harvest in return for lodging and board. The villagers were surprised strangers knew how to hold a scythe.

title: The lad with a dog
text: A lad with a dog passed through the camp and asked if you'd seen his sheep. The dog found it right afterwards under your wagon.

title: The murrain
text: Villagers speak of a cattle murrain in the next village. Everyone started avoiding strangers and your presence became awkward.

title: The doctor's visit
text: A wandering medic passed through the village selling potions. Half were worthless, half worked.

title: The stray
text: A scrawny mutt with a torn ear wandered into the camp. He ate the leftovers and stayed.

title: The evening prayer
text: Villagers gathered for evening prayer at a roadside shrine. The crew stood at the back not knowing what to do with their hands.

title: Smoke from the village
text: Smoke from the inn chimney drifted over the camp. Everyone grew hungry and half went to beg for scraps.

title: A sinister laugh
text: In the night someone laughed loudly behind the fence. Nobody saw him but everyone got chills.

title: The smith at the fair
text: The smith displayed new sickles at the fair. The crew bought two and learned to sharpen them.

title: First snow
text: The first snow covered the fields and roads. The village fell silent and the camp grew quiet and solemn.

title: The passing merchant
text: A merchant from Marienburg asked grain prices. The villagers named an inflated price and the crew got a commission for brokering.

title: The dead cow
text: A cow died in the night and the villagers couldn't bury it. The crew helped in exchange for some of the meat.

title: A small scuffle
text: Two drunks quarrelled over a spot by the fire. The crew threw both out and then ate their supper.

title: The ginger boy
text: A ginger lad from the village kept hanging round the camp. At last he admitted he'd like to join you. The crew laughed him off and gave him a loaf.

title: The potter
text: A village potter sold pots at bargain prices. The crew bought several pots and a few bowls.

title: An ill omen
text: A raven landed on a post by the road and croaked. The villagers spit over their left shoulders and the crew glances nervously at the sky.

title: The broken bridge
text: The bridge over the river cracked under a heavy wagon. The villagers set about repairing it and the crew joined, winning their goodwill.

title: Cunning snares
text: Villagers set snares for hares around the camp. Half your followers stepped into them by accident.

title: The village proverb
text: An old man by the fire spoke a proverb known to no one but everyone felt it held truth.

title: The shepherd with a flute
text: A shepherd played a flute by the fire and half the crew fell asleep to the sound. The best sleep in weeks.

title: The missing young ox
text: A young ox vanished from the herd and the owner promises a reward. The crew found it tied in the forest and knew who was behind it.

title: The animal fair
text: Horses and oxen were sold at the fair. The crew spotted a few bargains and one follower even bought a goat.

title: The stone shrine
text: A stone shrine with names of the dead engraved stood by the road. The crew paused a moment and lit a candle.

title: The gossiping neighbour
text: A gossiping neighbour told everyone about strangers in the camp. Half the village came to see and the other half locked their doors.

title: Crash of thunder
text: A great storm ruined half the village roofs. The crew helped with repairs and earned gratitude.

title: The lost ring
text: A peasant lost his wedding ring in the grass and asked for help searching. The crew found it within an hour and got a few shillings.

title: The indulgence fair
text: A church fair was held in the next village for a holy day. The market was full of people and the crew went out "collecting".

title: The rusty sword
text: A child found a rusty sword with an engraved crest in the field. The crew bought it for a handful of grain.

title: The bard storyteller
text: A wandering singer told of ancient heroes and bandits. The crew overheard a few interesting details about the area.

title: The strange boar
text: In the morning a dead boar with two heads was found in the field. The villagers drove everyone from the area and the crew gathered quickly.

title: The pigpen
text: Pigs escaped their pen and rampaged through the camp. Several villagers came to fetch them and stayed for supper.

title: The unlucky wanderer
text: A wanderer with a sore foot asked for shelter. The crew dressed it and he told of strange lights he saw in the forest at night.

title: The lost child
text: A child lost itself in the field and the crew found it. The parents wept for joy and gave everything they had in the pantry.

title: A shadow in the field
text: In the evening a shadow without an owner was seen in the field. The villagers fled in panic and the crew took the stores.

title: The broken clock
text: The clock on the church tower stopped and the villagers don't know the hour. Someone could fix it.

title: The clock mended
text: The clock runs again and the village held a thank-you feast for the crew. The reeve promised to repay with a favour.

title: The scarecrow
text: The scarecrow in the field stands in a different place every morning. The villagers fear it.

title: The scarecrow reveals
text: It turned out the scarecrow hid the entrance to an underground cellar. The crew found supplies and a few coins in it.

title: The small revolt
text: Villagers murmur against the steward and look for someone to lead them to the manor. They look at the crew.

title: The revolt breaks
text: The villagers marched on the manor with pitchforks. The crew can join, withdraw or sell the news to the steward.

title: The twins' visit
text: Two identical men arrived in the village asking for lodging. Each claims to be the true owner of an estate.

title: The true heir
text: It turned out one twin is an impostor. The true heir rewarded the crew generously.

title: The lost hunting dog
text: A beautiful hunting dog in a silver collar wanders around the camp. Someone will pay for its return.

title: The hunters look
text: A party of hunters in costly clothing asks about the lost dog. Their leader has a stern face and a generous purse.

title: A quarrel over a hen
text: Two housewives tore a hen between them and both got pecked. The whole village gathered and the crew collected the remaining hens.

title: The new reeve
text: The village elected a new reeve and celebrated till morning. The crew got several jugs of ale for "well-wishing".

title: A kindly day
text: The sun shone all day, birds sang and the villagers let the crew pass unhindered. Such a day rarely comes.

title: Snapped ropes
text: The ropes at the well snapped and the bucket fell down. The crew helped retrieve it for a few donations.

title: A windless morning
text: The air was still and smoke rose straight to the sky. Everyone noticed the birds fell silent.

title: Mercenaries marching through
text: A company of mercenaries marched through the village demanding food and lodging. The villagers gave all and trembled in fear.

title: The abandoned manor
text: An abandoned manor stands in the nearby forest. The crew looked at it from afar and one follower claimed he saw a candle in the window.

title: The cheerful trader
text: A cheerful salt trader stopped and told jokes. The crew bought some salt and laughed to tears.

title: Strange dogs
text: Strange dogs appeared at the edge of the camp and watched in silence. When someone threw a bone they left and never returned.

title: Youthful adventure
text: A young peasant confessed he'd like to leave the village and join someone who lives free. The crew gave him good advice and a loaf of bread.

title: The missing merchant
text: A merchant vanished on the road to the village and his wagon stands empty. The villagers fear to approach while the crew took inventory.

title: Work in the field
text: The crew helped with haymaking and the villagers repaid them. The camp had a hot meal and sweet milk at night.

title: The forgotten casket
text: A traveller left a casket in the inn and rode away. The innkeeper fears to open it and the crew could help.

title: The robbers' hut
text: An abandoned robbers' hut with leftover supplies was found in the forest. The villagers fear to go there but the crew doesn't.

title: A rainbow over the fields
text: After the storm a wide rainbow spread over the fields. The villagers said it was a sign of good crops and the crew felt good.

title: Smoke from the forest
text: Smoke rose from the forest as if someone were burning a fire. The villagers saw nobody and yet the smoke came every day.

title: The fair juggler
text: A juggler at the fair swallowed fire. The crew applauded and pickpockets had a good day.

title: A marital quarrel
text: Spouses' shouting came from one of the cottages. In the morning the husband had a black eye and the wife smiled broadly.

title: The mysterious parcel
text: Someone left a parcel wrapped in linen on the barn threshold. Inside was grain and a note reading "For a kind heart."

title: The village school
text: A teacher led children across the field showing them birds. The crew listened with interest and even learned a few names.

title: The lost letter
text: A letter blown from someone's hand by the wind landed in the camp. It's addressed to the captain of the local guards.

title: Evening songs
text: Villagers sang songs round the fires and the crew joined, surprising everyone with one follower's beautiful voice.

title: The apple thief
text: A boy was caught stealing apples in an orchard. The crew interceded for him and got a few apples as a reward.

title: The amulet seller
text: A wandering amulet seller praised his wares as protecting against all evil. The crew bought one just in case.

title: Honey
text: A beekeeper invited you to his apiary and offered honey. Everyone returned with sticky fingers and good humour.

title: The path through the marsh
text: A village guide showed a path through the marsh that officials avoid. The crew could slip away that way.

title: A village brawl
text: A brawl broke out at the inn because someone accused a neighbour of stealing a goat. The crew ate supper undisturbed.

title: The lost guard
text: A guard from the count lost his way at night and asked directions. The crew pointed him the wrong way and kept a straight face.

title: The scythe of death
text: Villagers performed a ritual against misfortune by hanging a scythe above the door. The crew watched uneasily.

title: The tale of the spectre
text: A grandfather told by the fire the story of a spectre that haunts the village every year. Today is that day.

title: The little cow
text: A peasant brought a cow asking for help with calving. The crew helped and got a week's worth of milk.

title: A woman's scream
text: In the morning a woman screamed. It turned out she found a spider in her bowl. Everyone laughed for a long time.

title: The door without a lock
text: One cottage door had no lock and villagers claimed nobody ever steals. The crew had to restrain themselves.

title: Visit from distant kin
text: A family from town arrived in the village in nice clothes with full purses. The crew watched them closely.

title: The lost goose
text: A goose with a mad stare ran round the camp honking. Someone caught it and for supper there was a roast.

title: Trouble with the well
text: The village well collapsed and the villagers had a water problem. The crew helped rebuild it.

title: The night hag
text: One follower woke screaming claiming something sat on his chest. The rest slept uneasily.

title: The lost hat
text: The wind carried off a town guest's hat. The crew caught it and returned it, winning his gratitude.

title: The village bard
text: A bard played the lute and told of the fall of old cities. The crew sat deep in thought and long afterwards spoke little.

title: The roadside inn
text: The roadside inn served exceptionally good ale at an indecently low price. Nobody asked why.

title: The farewell
text: An elderly follower decided to leave and settle in the countryside. Before leaving he left all his spoils to the crew.

title: Homecoming
text: One follower saw his home village from afar and fell to thinking. He was silent all day.

title: An evening by the fire
text: The crew sat by the fire reminiscing about old days. Everyone felt that together they could do anything.

title: The smell of roast meat
text: The smell of roast mutton drifted from the next village. A few followers went to "investigate" and returned well-fed.

title: The lost gold crown
text: A gold crown gleamed in the grass by the road. The crew picked it up although someone might be looking for it.

title: A quiet night
text: The night passed without incident. Everyone slept soundly and in the morning set out rested.
